title: Orbit Conditions for Conformal Validity in Replicated Matched-Block Experiments
banked_reason: Math review passed, but the single authorized D0.5 decision review found unresolved theorem-level comparator positioning and novelty below the field floor.

proof_attempt_summary: Discovery reached a fully discharged D0 core and a NO_ROOM maximality verdict; the final math referee passed. The single authorized D0.5 decision review did not clear the field novelty floor because two theorem-level comparator gaps remained, so the revise loop was stopped before F and the verified D-stage artifact was banked.
tldr: For iid replicated matched-block experiments with a known invariant assignment law, equality of calibration and target mass on every member orbit is necessary and sufficient for universal armwise score-law equality. Observable selectors are normalized and supported on the requested realized arm for assignments with positive design mass, with auxiliary draws conditional on assignment; assignments outside that support receive zero integrated weight. A finite stacked linear program finds a common two-arm selector under exact balance, quotient likelihood-ratio weighting gives armwise conformal validity under orbit overlap, and ordinary ranks admit exact-balance, total-variation, disjoint-support, and matched-pair certificates. Separately, a preorder and memoized four-cell algorithm exactly evaluates \(\Gamma_{M,\alpha,\boldsymbol\varepsilon}(w)\) only for the deterministic bounded orbit-constant-score audit submodel. It retains one coherent target and within-replicate cross-arm dependence but is not a full-model joint-inclusion or causal effect-set coverage theorem.
gap: Finite-group testing and group-symmetry prediction establish validity from invariance, while causal and cluster-randomized conformal work studies counterfactual or treatment-effect targets under its own assignment regimes. Those scopes do not themselves decide whether an assignment-based calibration selector and a deployment target induce the same score law on a declared finite orbit quotient. The computational literature treats general discrete rectangular probabilities, simultaneous conformal error control, multi-target error allocation, or structured-set volume, all of which differ from this paper's restricted deterministic orbit-score audit functional.
fill: The orbit-mass equivalence supplies a necessity witness as well as sufficiency, the stacked linear program supplies a computable common selector, quotient likelihood ratios supply weighted armwise validity despite member-level singularity, and clipping plus Bonferroni produces one common-member effect guarantee. The asymmetric preorder evaluator preserves the coherent common target and within-replicate cross-arm dependence and reports exact time and memory charges for the paper-defined deterministic audit functional, while explicitly excluding stochastic conditional residual scores from that frontier.
